title: Select Committee on Deliberate Online Falsehoods – Causes, Consequences and Countermeasures
what_it_is: Select Committee on Deliberate Online Falsehoods – Causes, Consequences and Countermeasures

sections.label: Global disinformation campaigns
sections.summary: Countries worldwide have faced organised deliberate disinformation campaigns by state and non-state actors aimed at destabilising countries and interfering with democratic processes.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Countries across the world have been the subject of organised deliberate disinformation campaigns − conducted both by state actors, targeted at destabilising other countries, and also non-state actors and they spread the falsehoods deliberately to both interfere with the democratic processes within countries and to also destabilise and undermine institutions within a specific country Most Members, if not all, would have come across these examples reported almost on a daily basis in the media.

sections.label: Select Committee on online falsehoods
sections.summary: The speaker asks Parliament to appoint a Select Committee to examine causes and consequences of deliberate online falsehoods and required countermeasures in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Ultimately, if left unchecked, such deliberate spread of online falsehoods can undermine trust in the country, in the institutions, in democracy and affect social cohesion.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, I am asking Parliament to appoint a Select Committee, to examine and report on the causes and consequences of deliberate online falsehoods; and the countermeasures that will be required to prevent and combat them in Singapore.

sections.label: Select Committee composition
sections.summary: The proposed Select Committee has 10 members, nine Government MPs and one Opposition MP, with one Government MP replaced by a Nominated MP.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The composition of the Select Committee, we suggest, the default position is for 10 members − nine Government MPs and one MP from the Opposition bench − but we propose replacing one of the Government MPs with a Nominated MP, to have more diversity.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Terms of Reference have been broadly framed, intentionally.

sections.label: Eastern Sun Hong Kong funding
sections.summary: The Eastern Sun was exposed by the Government for receiving HKD$8 million from a communist intelligence agency from Hong Kong.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In the same period, the Eastern Sun was exposed by the Government for receiving HKD$8 million from a communist intelligence agency from Hong Kong.

sections.label: TRS convictions and Russian content
sections.summary: The two TRS editors were convicted of sedition and MCI cancelled the TRS website's Class Licence; 126 million Americans were exposed to Russian-linked content.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The two editors of the TRS were convicted in court for sedition and the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) cancelled the Class Licence of the TRS website.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: It was estimated that 126 million Americans were exposed to 80,000 pieces of Russian-linked content targeted to influence the outcome of the 2016 US Presidential Elections.

sections.label: Singaporeans encountering inaccurate online news
sections.summary: A Government poll in May 2017 showed one in four Singaporeans frequently come across online news that was not fully accurate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: A Government poll in May 2017 showed that one in four Singaporeans frequently come across online news that was not fully accurate.

sections.label: Select Committee on online falsehood
sections.summary: The speaker supports a Motion to convene a Select Committee on online falsehood, citing the need for an inclusive approach and a broader national conversation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Mechanisms need to be put in place to respond swiftly to these falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: So, we need an inclusive approach to address these issues holistically, involving not only the public sector, but the private and people sectors too.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: And we need a broader national conversation about this issue so everyone has a shared understanding of the threat and a sense of ownership about the solution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Hence, Sir, I fully support this Motion to convene a Select Committee on online falsehood.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This will allow us to consult widely and tap on the collective wisdom of the community and stakeholders.

sections.label: Singapore social media penetration
sections.summary: Seventy-seven percent of Singaporeans are active social media users, placing Singapore third globally in social media penetration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Seventy-seven percent of Singaporeans are active social media users, placing us third globally, in terms of social media penetration.

sections.label: Cry wolf syndrome and foreign laws
sections.summary: Repeated online falsehoods can cause a cry wolf syndrome, and Germany, France, the UK and Ireland have enacted laws to limit fake news.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Repeated instances of deliberate online falsehoods can also have costs as it can lead to a "cry wolf syndrome", whereby when a real emergency strikes, no one reacts because everybody is accustomed to thinking it is false news.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In recent months, several countries, Germany, France, the UK and Ireland have moved quickly to protect themselves by enacting laws to limit fake news and punish purveyors and websites who either disseminate or fail to take down fake news.

sections.label: Grounds for convening Select Committee
sections.summary: Online falsehoods' wide ramifications, rapid transmission and disruption to security, financial stability and religious harmony warrant convening a Select Committee.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The problems posed by online falsehoods with the wide ramifications across all sections of society, rapid speed of transmission and seriousness of disruption to security, financial stability and religious harmony – are all serious enough to warrant convening a Select Committee.

sections.label: False news in Punggol constituency
sections.summary: False news of a collapsed HDB roof in Punggol led public agencies to despatch vehicles and manpower, wasting public resources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I have personally witnessed how false news can cause damage in my constituency, Punggol.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: There was news that the roof of a Housing and Development Board (HDB) block had collapsed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Although this news was deleted after half an hour, public agencies had already despatched vehicles and manpower to the site within that half an hour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: False news has caused the wastage of public resources which could have been used on things that need them more.

sections.label: Free speech and Select Committee
sections.summary: The speaker says freedom of speech must be protected by law and supports the Motion to set up a Select Committee on online falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Freedom of speech must be protected by the law.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, I support the Motion to set up a Select Committee to examine ways to tackle online falsehoods.

sections.label: Online misinformation global trend ranking
sections.summary: The 2014 World Economic Forum ranked the rapid spread of online misinformation as the 10th top global trend.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: An indication of the severity of the spread of online falsehoods was given at the World Economic Forum in 2014, where the rapid spread of misinformation online was considered the 10th top trend of global significance.

sections.label: Telecommunications Act false message offence
sections.summary: The Telecommunications Act makes transmitting a known false message an offence, but this provision has been ineffective against online falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: For instance, under the Telecommunications Act, it is an offence to transmit a message knowing that it is false.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, in practice, this provision has been ineffective in properly addressing the spread of online falsehoods.

sections.label: Facebook disputed warning labels
sections.summary: In December 2016, Facebook began showing a disputed warning next to articles third-party checking websites called fake news.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In December 2016, Facebook began showing a "disputed" warning next to articles that third-party checking websites said were fake news.

sections.label: NUS SUTD hackathon on falsehoods
sections.summary: In October 2017, NUS, SUTD, Google and the Media Literacy Council, supported by The Straits Times, held a hackathon on online falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In October 2017, the National University of Singapore (NUS), the Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD), Google and the Media Literacy Council, supported by The Straits Times, organised a hackathon to solve the problem of online falsehoods.

sections.label: Select Committee motion on falsehoods
sections.summary: The speaker says fighting online falsehoods must be a concerted effort and welcomes the Motion for a Select Committee to examine it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The effort in fighting online falsehoods therefore has to be a concerted effort.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am very glad therefore that this Motion has been put forth for a Select Committee to examine the various aspects of online falsehoods and propose some measures.

sections.label: Legislation within multi-pronged approach
sections.summary: The speaker asks if the Government could consider legislation as part of a wider, more multi-pronged approach including public education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Although, legislation would regulate conduct in relation to the spread of online falsehoods, I believe there are other efforts that could be put in place including public education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I would therefore ask if the Government could consider legislation as part of a wider, more multi-pronged approach.

sections.label: Select Committee on online falsehoods
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes a proposal to form a Select Committee to study online falsehoods and propose measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: We must work as one country in order to achieve an effective outcome.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Hence, I welcome the proposal to form a Select Committee to study the spread of online falsehoods and propose measures to overcome them.

sections.label: Balancing legislation against online falsehoods
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Select Committee will balance national security and public order with discussion and media reporting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We do not want a heavy handed approach that will be root out constructive, though at times, disagreeable voices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I hope that the Select Committee will consider, if there are to be new legislation against deliberate online falsehoods, that it needs to balance the interest of protecting national security and preserving public order with the interests of: (a) enabling individuals to have meaningful discussions on issues of concern, including Government policies, without fear of having action taken against them, and (b) enabling the media, both professional and citizen journalists, to report on such issues of concern.

sections.label: Existing laws as starting point
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Select Committee to start from present laws such as the Broadcasting Notification and Telecommunications Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, I would urge the Select Committee to look at what our present law provisions have as a starting point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Such laws include the Broadcasting (Class Licence) Notification or section 45 of the Telecommunications Act, and specific laws such as the Administration of Justice (Protection) Act, the Protection from Harassment Act, the Sedition Act, and the tort of defamation.

sections.label: Existing laws called effective
sections.summary: The speaker says a falsehood was quickly quashed and not circulated, showing existing laws have been effective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And, in fact, based on what I have observed, very quickly, that piece of falsehood was quashed and the public understood and knew and did not circulate it anymore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I think this demonstrates that our existing laws and provision have been effective.

sections.label: Media literacy at all levels
sections.summary: The speaker says media literacy is important and should be inculcated in schools, community, workplaces and home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Media literacy is important and should be inculcated in all levels of society: in schools, in community set-ups, in workplaces and even at home.

sections.label: Fact-checking, consultation, minority reports
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Select Committee considers independent fact-checking bodies, more consultation time, and minority reports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The earlier when information is being shared, without prejudicing justice or national security concerns that would help people to know and be able to clear the air.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also hope that the Select Committee would also look at multiple independent fact-checking bodies that would allow the public to fact-check, cross reference so that they can make decisions themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask the Select Committee, when calling out for public engagement, again, to allow more time for consultation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A recent incident was the draft of the Film Act where we had only nine days to make that submission and we had to appeal for another two more weeks for that submission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And I hope that this will not happen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But at the same time, I wonder would the Select Committee consider, because this is an issue of such a broad concern, that there may be disagreement within the Select Committee in terms of what to do, that there should be provisions for minority reports in the Select Committee report.

sections.label: Automated election tweets on Twitter
sections.summary: The Green Paper states 36,746 Twitter accounts generated about 1.4 million automated, election-related tweets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is because of the ubiquitous nature of online falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I refer to paragraph 14(b) of the Green Paper to put things into perspective: 36,746 Twitter accounts generated approximately 1.4 million automated, election-related tweets.

sections.label: Younger Singaporeans' optimism bias study
sections.summary: An NUS Communications and New Media Department and Institute of Policy Studies study found younger Singaporeans have an optimism bias.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: According to a study done by the Communications and New Media Department at NUS and the Institute of Policy Studies, younger Singaporeans have an optimism bias.

sections.label: Italy minister funeral false caption
sections.summary: In Italy, a government Minister's funeral appearance was falsely captioned as mourning a mafia boss.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For example, in Italy, a government Minister's appearance at a funeral was falsely captioned to make it appear as if she was mourning a mafia boss.

sections.label: False Rohingya images on Twitter
sections.summary: A Straits Times article reported false Twitter images purporting to show Rohingyas persecuting Hindus in Rakhine province.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A Straits Times article on India’s fight against fake news reported that false images had been circulated on Twitter purporting to show Rohingyas persecuting Hindus in the Rakhine province, where the Muslim Rohingyas have been fleeing alleged persecution.

sections.label: Falsehoods hampering democracy examples
sections.summary: Brexit and US and UK election examples show falsehoods may hamper democracy, and the motion refers regulation principles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: An example of how falsehoods may hamper democracy can be seen in the Brexit situation where there was a misleading poll with shaky extrapolation that caused people to think that millions of Turkish people would move to the UK if it voted to remain in the European Union.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Another example is how, during the recent elections in the US and UK, supporters of a particular candidate or party had been encouraged to vote via invalid methods or on an invalid day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Today, Sir, the motion is to refer the question of which principles should apply to the regulation of deliberate online falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: If falsehoods continue to influence the minds of people across sensitive issues, such as our multi-racial identity and our national security, then our unity will be at stake.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As stated in the Green paper and reinforced by the Ministers today, online falsehoods, or '"fake news", as it is more commonly known, can have very serious and debilitating consequences for societies.

sections.label: Singapore courses on fake news
sections.summary: Three polytechnics and universities in Singapore introduced and modified courses emphasising fake news, teaching credibility checks, cross-referencing and authoritative sources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Three polytechnics and universities in Singapore have recently introduced and modified courses to include emphasis on fake news.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Students will be taught to do credibility checks on sources, cross-referencing and the use of authoritative sources.

sections.label: Opinion pieces undermining sensitive issues
sections.summary: Opinion pieces that can undermine sensitive issues or negotiations may be more damaging than fake news from foreign sources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To me, opinion pieces that can undermine sensitive issues or negotiations can be even more damaging than fake news from foreign sources.

sections.label: Dartmouth study on news consumption
sections.summary: Dartmouth College analysed real and fake news consumption of thousands of adults before the 2016 US election, with Dr Brendan noting social media algorithms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Dartmouth College recently analysed the real and fake news consumption of thousands of adults in the lead up to the 2016 US election.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The research shows that most lies and false rumours online go nowhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, the key researcher, Dr Brendan, notes that social media companies have algorithms that "dangerously effective at identifying memes that are well-adapted to surviving, and these also tend to be rumours and conspiracy theories that are hardest to correct".

sections.label: Support for Select Committee
sections.summary: The speaker supports creating a Select Committee on Deliberate Online Falsehoods due to danger from state and non-state actors weaponising disinformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In view of the danger that certain state and non-state actors pose, by weaponising disinformation into fake news, I support the creation of the Select Committee on Deliberate Online Falsehoods.

sections.label: Commission studies on Singaporeans' views
sections.summary: Detailed and prolonged studies should be commissioned to understand how Singaporeans gather views and how social media shape them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Two, we should commission detailed and prolonged studies to understand how Singaporeans gather their views, and how social media shape their views.

sections.label: Labour Movement supports Select Committee
sections.summary: The Labour Movement supports a Select Committee to study deliberate online falsehoods and recommend responses, proposing diverse members from community and digital media.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With the rise in technology and digitisation, the online space has been widening and is certainly one area of concern for every right-minded people and organisations, including the Labour Movement, given the multinational, multi-racial, multi-religious composition of the people and members that we have.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I support the appointment of a Select Committee to study the issue of deliberate online falsehoods, that is, fake news, and make appropriate and well-balanced recommendations as to how, as a nation, we should respond and how to cultivate the values of accountability and responsibility, especially when posting materials on social media.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There is a fine line between satires, deliberate online falsehood or differing yet genuine opinions that may not resonate with the State's views.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I propose that the Select Committee comprise different parties in the community and professionals from the digital media sector with relevant knowledge and experience.

sections.label: NTUC FairPrice survey scam example
sections.summary: A recent online survey scam claiming NTUC FairPrice rewarded customers with a $400 gift card voucher demonstrates the spread of falsehoods online.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The recent online survey scam that NTUC FairPrice was rewarding customers with a $400 gift card voucher in celebration of its 45th anniversary is a clear example to demonstrate the spread of falsehoods online.

sections.label: French law on false content
sections.summary: The proposed French law requires websites to publish sponsors' identities and lets judges remove content and close sites publishing false information.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The proposed law in France requires websites to make public the identities of those who sponsor content.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It also provides for emergency procedures introduced during elections, providing judges the ultimate power to remove content, close websites that publish false information or fake news.

sections.label: MCI survey on falsehoods
sections.summary: A June 2017 MCI survey found about 25% shared information later found false, two-thirds could not recognise falsehoods, and half were confident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: A June 2017 survey by the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) found that around 25% of respondents shared information that they later discovered to be false.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Around two-thirds could not recognise falsehoods when they first saw it and only half were confident of their ability to recognise falsehoods.

sections.label: FairPrice online falsehoods
sections.summary: The NTUC FairPrice CEO says FairPrice faced online falsehoods claiming it sells halal pork and plastic rice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Declaring my interest as the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of NTUC FairPrice, FairPrice, too, has had its fair share of Online Falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: So, according to information online, FairPrice, for example, sells "halal pork" and also "plastic rice".

sections.label: FairPrice police report on rice
sections.summary: Last year FairPrice filed a police report over viral claims that its house brand jasmine fragrant rice is made of plastic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Just last year, FairPrice also had to file a police report over viral claims that its house brand jasmine fragrant rice is made of plastic.

sections.label: Duty against online falsehoods
sections.summary: The passage rejects the assumption that people change their minds with new facts and states a duty to keep public discourse from being crowded out by falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In short: False assumption 2 – people change their minds when presented with new facts, which leads me to Principle 2 – We have a duty to ensure, to the extent possible, that the marketplace of public discourse is not crowded out by falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: To do this, we need to actively invest in any efforts to discern, filter, contain, disrupt or even punish deliberate Online Falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Perhaps, the solutions may be both legislative and relying on market forces.

sections.label: Israeli social network legislation
sections.summary: Israel has proposed legislation requiring social networks to monitor for incitement to terrorism and remove it or pay fines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Israel, for example, has proposed legislation requiring social networks to take reasonable measures to monitor their platforms for incitement to terrorism and to remove such incitement, or be liable to pay fines.

sections.label: Legislation powers against falsehoods
sections.summary: Legislation can criminalise falsehood publication, mandate removal of such news from platforms and websites, and ensure readers access facts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Some examples of what legislation can do include making falsehood publication a criminal offence, mandating the removal of such news from platforms and websites, and/or ensuring that readers have access to facts.

sections.label: Heavy-handed legislation backfire risk
sections.summary: Heavy-handed legislation may backfire on the Government acting as judge, jury and executioner of credible information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Heavy-handed legislation may backfire on the Government acting as judge, jury and executioner of what constitutes credible information.

sections.label: Select Committee discussion of problems
sections.summary: A Select Committee allows thorough discussion of problems such as social media responsibilities, public education, and websites' duty over deliberate falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Having a Select Committee will allow for a thorough discussion of the problems posed by this issue, such as responsibilities of social media and tech companies’ platforms, how to educate the public to discern news, the duty that websites have towards using deliberate falsehoods to attract more hits and to drive revenue.

sections.label: Select Committee best way forward
sections.summary: A Select Committee with broad terms of reference as proposed in this Motion is the best way of working these out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: A Select Committee with the broad terms of reference as proposed in this Motion is the best way of working these out.

sections.label: Universities, fake news, Green Paper
sections.summary: The speaker points to universities on fake news, supports the Select Committee Motion, and notes Ministries' recognition of the Green Paper requiring multi-stakeholder response.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the course of this speech, I would like to point this House to what is going on in the universities as far as fake news is concerned.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I support the Motion of a Select Committee, Sir, to address this problem, as well as the Ministries' recognition of the Green Paper that this problem requires a multi-stakeholder response.

sections.label: Defining fake news
sections.summary: The passage asks how we define what is or is not fake news.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, how do we define, what is or what is not fake news?

sections.label: Understandings of fake news
sections.summary: Recent understandings of fake news or online falsehoods focus on news low in veracity and high in intention to mislead.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The most recent understandings of fake news or online falsehoods focus on pieces of news that are low in veracity and high in the intention to mislead.

sections.label: Pre-emptive legal measures
sections.summary: Pre-emptive measures should be the main focus of legal solutions, as false information can inflict lasting damage even if later disproved.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Pre-emptive measures, which is what the Select Committee would be thinking about, should be the main focus of legal solutions that we are putting together, as false information and fake news can inflict lasting damage long after it has been disseminated, even if this news is subsequently disproved.

sections.label: Digital literacy for vulnerable segments
sections.summary: Enhancing digital literacy among the elderly and youth should be part of the solution, as they may benefit from the truth.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Enhancing digital literacy amongst vulnerable segments of society should also be part of the solution, namely the elderly and the youth who are given false information may benefit from the truth.

sections.label: Network of fact-checkers
sections.summary: A network of fact-checkers could be set up.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A network, Sir, of fact-checkers, as many of us have spoken about, could be set up.

sections.label: Media coverage and fact-checking websites
sections.summary: Media outlets should consider critical coverage of disinformation, and such networks can be state-driven, like the UK's "Factually" and a US website.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Media outlets should consider including critical coverage of disinformation just to explain that this is not the case and to set the record straight.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These networks can be state-driven, such as the local Government website "Factually", which is set up in the UK, which is a fact-checking website set up by the British parliament as well as another website in the US set up for the same purpose.

sections.label: Need for new legislation
sections.summary: The question of whether a new piece of legislation is really needed should be looked into carefully by the Select Committee.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: His question, I guess, would be: do we really need a new piece of legislation?

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I think the Select Committee should look into this question very carefully.

sections.label: Brexit online falsehoods immigration
sections.summary: In 2016, online falsehoods about immigration before the Brexit referendum claimed 12 million Turks would enter the UK if it stayed in the EU.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In 2016, online falsehoods were spread about immigration in the lead-up to the "Brexit" referendum, which fuelled support for "Brexit" by claiming that the UK will see an influx of 12 million Turks if it remained in the EU.

sections.label: Halal certification terrorism false claim
sections.summary: In 2015, companies getting halal certification were targeted by a campaign claiming halal certification funds terrorism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In 2015, companies that get products halal certified were targets of a campaign that claimed that halal certification funds terrorism.

sections.label: Mosul al-Nuri mosque false claim
sections.summary: In 2017, it claimed a US-led coalition airstrike destroyed Mosul's al-Nuri mosque, when ISIS had destroyed it with explosives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In 2017, it claimed that Mosul’s famed al-Nuri mosque was blown up by a US-led coalition airstrike, when in fact, ISIS had destroyed the mosque themselves, using explosives.

sections.label: Germany unlawful content takedown fines
sections.summary: Some countries such as Germany have laws to take down unlawful content and systemic breaches, with fines of €50 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Some countries, such as Germany, have laws to take down unlawful content and systemic breaches that can result in fines of €50 million.

sections.label: Foreign influence risk small connected population
sections.summary: Given Singapore's small size and highly connected population, it is at risk of foreign influence and intervention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Given our small size and highly connected population, we are at risk of foreign influence and intervention.

sections.label: Select Committee consensus online falsehoods
sections.summary: One key priority of the Select Committee is gaining consensus among Singaporeans on defining online falsehoods and possibly refining OB markers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One of the key priorities, I feel, of the Select Committee is to gain consensus among Singaporeans on how we define online falsehoods, and perhaps it may be time to refine and update our OB markers for the future.

sections.label: Germany and New Zealand laws
sections.summary: Germany has legislation to close platforms displaying illegal content with fines up to €50 million, while New Zealand courts can order a right of reply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Some countries like Germany have introduced legislation to close down platforms that display content that break the law, and such offences can carry fines up to €50 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: New Zealand is taking an approach under its laws that allows its Courts to order a right of reply to correct any false information about an individual.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim community countering falsehoods
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Malay/Muslim community, including leaders, online entrepreneurs and the man-in-the-street, will give suggestions to counter online falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this regard, I hope that the Malay/Muslim community can also contribute and play a role, whether they are community and religious leaders, online entrepreneurs or the man-in-the-street, and that all of us will give suggestions and ideas about ways to counter online falsehoods.

sections.label: Singapore riots casualties
sections.summary: The riots in Singapore lasted seven days, resulting in four people dead and 80 injured.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The riots in Singapore lasted for seven whole days resulting in four people dead and 80 injured.

sections.label: The Real Singapore website earnings
sections.summary: The couple who created The Real Singapore website made more than $500,000 from advertising and bought a house in Australia.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, the couple who created The Real Singapore website made more than $500,000 from advertising and bought a house in Australia; $500,000.

sections.label: Russian fake news readership
sections.summary: The US found fake news from Russia and East Europe was read by 150 million people and could have influenced the US Presidential Election.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The US has found out that fake news from Russia and East Europe had been read by 150 million people and this could have influenced the US Presidential Election.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If other countries intend to use fake news to influence our five million people and destroy our racial harmony and stability, it should not be too difficult.

sections.label: Support for Select Committee on fake news
sections.summary: The speaker supports establishing a Select Committee to study tackling fake news, and asks whether the Act undermines free speech or targets opposition critics.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Not doing so is akin to gambling with Singaporeans' life and livelihood.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, I support the establishment of the Select Committee to study carefully how to tackle fake news.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, will this Act undermine online freedom of speech?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, will this Act be used against the opposition parties and people who criticise the Government?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, I support the establishment of the Select Committee to gather feedback from various sectors, to be debated later in Parliament.

sections.label: MPs and NMPs support Motion
sections.summary: Seven MPs and four NMPs spoke and all supported the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Seven Members of Parliament (MPs) and four Nominated MPs (NMPs) have spoken, all supported the Motion.

sections.label: Combating falsehoods and free speech
sections.summary: The speaker says the Select Committee will consider the form of measures, and that combating falsehoods is not contrary to free speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think Mr Zaqy Mohamad, Mr Kok Heng Leun also made similar points.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think the precise form and ambit of any measure to be proposed, including legislation, is something for the Select Committee to consider.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But I think most Singaporeans would agree that free online debate − including the expression of critical comments − should not be predicated on deliberate falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: My own view is that combating falsehoods is not contrary to the exercise of freedom of speech.

sections.label: Select Committee membership and experts
sections.summary: The Select Committee will comprise Members of Parliament and can hear from experts from different areas and sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Select Committee will comprise Members of Parliament but they can hear from experts from different areas, sectors, including the media and other sectors.

sections.label: Broad terms of reference
sections.summary: The terms of reference were crafted broadly so different perspectives can come in for the Select Committee to consider.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But those are questions for the Select Committee to consider more fully when it starts work.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That is why we have crafted the terms of reference broadly, so that different perspectives can come in.

sections.label: Stakeholders invited to come forward
sections.summary: The speaker hopes experts, media, technology companies and the public will come forward so Singaporeans better understand what is at stake.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For my part, I hope that different stakeholders will come forward – experts, media, technology companies and the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Hopefully, the process will help Singaporeans better understand what is at stake.

sections.label: Division vote result
sections.summary: The division recorded 80 Ayes, no Noes and no abstentions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Division taken: Ayes, 80; Noes, Nil; Abstention, Nil

sentences.text: There are 80 "Ayes, zero "Noes", and zero "Abstentions".
